verdicts.rationale: This is the exact same concept appearing under slightly different naming conventions.
Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors are often used after detecting the issue with tests like the White test.
The Breusch-Pagan test assumes a specific parametric form for heteroskedasticity, whereas the White test is general and does not require specifying that form.
Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors are directly built to solve the inference failure caused by heteroskedasticity.
The White test detects heteroskedasticity, which helps determine whether you might need to use methods like weighted least squares if the form is identified.
Weighted least squares is designed directly as a solution to remedy heteroskedasticity when its form is known.
Weighted least squares restores BLUE properties by transforming a model with heteroskedasticity into one that satisfies homoskedastic Gauss-Markov assumptions.
